title: Telegram Interaction Platform — production verification
scope: TG-018 through TG-029 (notification policy, rich cards, deep links, attachments, reliability, settings UI, telemetry, security hardening, production verification, dogfood posture, evidence, freeze) plus the TG-030 webhook tunnel extension

covers: vertical slice: Telegram -> principal -> workspace -> execution -> reply
card + coalescer + deep link + telemetry projection

security matrix: spoofed secret, replayed callback, expired pairing token, tampered deep link, cross-workspace, stale/post-terminal approval, revoked principal, disabled integration, command injection
TG-018 notification policy, filters, quiet hours, normalization, delivery projection
TG-019 execution cards and TG-021 attachment policy/validation
TG-020 signed deep-link build/parse/verify, tamper and expiry
TG-022 failure classification, backoff, rate limiting, coalescing
TG-027 dogfood posture: dogfood parks Telegram, full/default activate it
webhook tunnel lifecycle, public-URL validation, provider output parsing, webhook registration consent
ENOENT translated to TunnelProviderUnavailableError; isCommandAvailable probes
banner-link regression: non-tunnel HTTPS URLs (terms of service) are ignored; only known tunnel hosts accepted
DNS-readiness gate before setWebhook; registration retry; re-registration on an active tunnel
tunnel settings endpoints: status, enable/disable, provider validation, availability, configuration persistence

limitations: Executed against a dirty working tree; the recorded commit is the parent HEAD, not a commit containing this work.
Full-repository `pnpm build` / `pnpm test` / `pnpm lint:check` were not executed as part of this run; only the telegram-integration project and the two apps/api Telegram suites were built and run.
The Settings UI (TG-023) was type-verified, not visually regression-tested; no Playwright baseline was regenerated.
No live Telegram Bot API call was made; verification uses in-process services and a fake execution backend.
